title: Cost Skein Visualizer: strand-based token attribution & export patterns
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design a new console panel called 'Cost Skein Visualizer' that represents token-level cost flows as interwoven strands across routes, sessions, and SKUs. The goal is to give engineers and finance users a single interactive view for attribution, delta analysis, and exportable artifacts. The skein metaphor supports three core interactions: 1) Strand focus: click a strand to isolate token origin (prompt vs completion vs tools), model variant, and quantization tier; 2) Crosscut: create slices across time or customer segments to compare marginal unit cost and latency; 3) Stitch/export: define export rules that flatten skein strands into role-aware CSVs or compact JSONL for billing reconciliation. This ticket covers the high-level flow prototype, accessibility considerations, pricing UI patterns for showing blended vs SKU-aware unit rates, and a compact export UX for large-volume customers.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype screens exist for three skein states: overview, focused strand, and crosscut compare
Export modal supports at least two formats (role-aware CSV and compressed JSONL) with selectable columns and time granularity
Pricing pattern component shows blended unit cost and expandable SKU breakdown with inline help text
Design tokens and color palette accessible at AA contrast for strand colors
Interaction spec documents how stray request fallbacks are represented and how estimated vs actual cost is displayed

design_decisions: Use 'strand' visual abstraction rather than stacked bars to emphasize flow and re-use across sessions
Offer two export compression levels: full (JSONL with payload hashes) and minimal (CSV with token counts and unit rates)
Blended pricing shown by default; SKU-aware toggle available inline to avoid overwhelming new users
Inline help links to a pricing glossary to reduce cognitive load for billing teams
open_questions: How should multi-model fanout be represented when a single request fans out to several model variants?
Should we allow custom stitching rules to persist as named templates for customers?
Can engineering provide estimated vs actual token counts per strand for historical windows older than 90 days?

Task 1: Identify the top 3 cost drivers for a given 7-day window

Collect SUS and open feedback; iterate in next cycle
